1	# Voice
2	
3	## Tone Principles
4	
5	NINEONELABS copy should be:
6	
7	- Bold: confident, not arrogant.
8	- Experimental: surprising only when it improves clarity.
9	- Precise: no filler.
10	- Warm at scale: collaborative without becoming casual.
11	- Proof-driven: grounded in shipped work, systems, or measurable outcomes.
12	
13	Avoid:
14	
15	- generic agency speak
16	- empty inspiration
17	- technical name-dropping without outcome
18	- space fantasy without service clarity
19	- corporate boilerplate
20	- overly polite sales language
21	- trend-chasing AI/tool language
22	
23	## Korean Copy
24	
25	- Use formal polite public-facing Korean.
26	- Keep sentences short.
27	- Prefer `함께`, `여정`, `브랜드`, `설계`, `경험`, `구조`, `증명`.
28	- Avoid `솔루션`, `최고의`, `최적의`, `고객님`.
29	- A Korean line break must preserve grammar and meaning when each line is read alone.
30	
31	## English Copy
32	
33	- Display copy may use ALL CAPS or title case depending on visual role.
34	- English must be understandable to Korean readers at a glance.
35	- Prefer short, common words over clever phrasing.
36	- For clear utility/proof sections, use direct nouns first: `SERVICES`, `WORKS`, `PARTNERS`, `CLIENTS`, `CONTACT`.
37	- Do not force journey or space metaphors into section titles when the section job is already obvious.
38	- Avoid repeated `WE... / WE... / WE...` headline patterns unless repetition is the concept.
39	- Do not stack the same English opening shape across adjacent homepage sections when a stronger noun-led or outcome-led alternative exists.
40	- Vary openings with nouns, objects, outcomes, or fragments: `NEW WEBSITES`, `REAL WORK`, `FROM TEST TO LAUNCH`, `DESIGNED TO PROVE`, `BUILT THROUGH FRICTION`.
41	- Use `NINEONELABS` for public brand display. Use `nineonelabs` only in technical/code contexts.
42	
43	## Journey Language Temperature Guide
44	
45	NINEONELABS의 여정/우주 언어는 제거 대상이 아니다. 섹션의 감정적 역할에 따라 온도를 조절한다.
46	
47	| Temperature | Sections | Journey/Space Language | Concreteness Required |
48	|---|---|---|---|
49	| Poetic (뜨거움) | `intro`, `hero`, `contact` | Full strength — the brand voice lives here | Slogan or direction-setting is enough |
50	| Balanced (따뜻함) | `introAction`, `story`, `who`, `partners` | Use as context, must land on a real role or result | At least one role, outcome, or action |
51	| Concrete (시원함) | `why`, `services`, `portfolio` | Brand tone only — lead with capability or deliverable | Specific tools, outputs, or proof required |
52	
53	Rules:
54	- `여정` is a core brand word. Use it in Poetic sections freely. In Balanced sections, ground it with a concrete digital word (`웹`, `화면`, `구조`, `설계`).
55	- Removing `여정` from a Poetic section and replacing it with transactional language is always wrong.
56	- Contact is Poetic temperature. The CTA button label is direct (`Contact`, `Works`); the body copy stays in the brand voice.
57	- Maximum 4 instances of `여정` per page: 2 in Poetic sections, 2 in Balanced sections.
58	- The rule "every space metaphor must land on a concrete digital outcome" applies to Balanced and Concrete sections. Poetic sections may end at the metaphor when the slogan carries the meaning.
59	
60	## Rhythm Rules
61	
62	Do not let consecutive sections use the same copy shape.
63	
64	| Scene | Copy Job | Suggested Shape |
65	|---|---|---|
66	| `intro` | invite | short English headline + 2 Korean lines |
67	| `introAction` | align and move | two short beats, each with a different verb |
68	| `hero` | land the slogan | slogan + short clarifying Korean line |
69	| `story` | reveal attitude | brand belief + concrete Korean proof |
70	
71	## Bad Copy And Better Direction
72	
73	| Do Not Write | Better Direction |
74	|---|---|
75	| `우리는 최고의 웹 경험을 제공합니다` | `우리가 만든 웹은 사용자가 스크롤을 멈추게 합니다` |
76	| `Innovative digital solutions` | `Scroll-triggered 3D brand story, built in Three.js` |
77	| `We are passionate about design` | `We ship design systems that work across 5 touchpoints` |
78	| `We use cutting-edge technology` | `Three.js, GSAP, and TypeScript embedded in the site you actually ship` |
79	| `브랜드의 가치를 높여드립니다` | `브랜드를 한 문장으로 설명할 수 있을 때, 설계가 끝난 겁니다` |
80	
81	## Web Agency Copy Rules
82	
83	- Talk about results, not tools.
84	- Frame process as journey language only when it supports a concrete digital outcome.
85	- Every space metaphor must land on web, app, branding, UI/UX, maintenance, proof, or action.
86	
87	## Skill Label Rules
88	
89	- Skill labels in `why` may be short and technical, but descriptions must stay clear and outcome-aware.
90	- Use skill labels as proof signals, not service descriptions.
91	- Prefer compact pairs such as `THREE.JS / INTERACTIVE WEB`, `GSAP / MOTION & ANIMATION`, `CMS SYSTEM / CONTENT CONTROL`.
92	- If a skill description needs a full sentence, it probably belongs in `services` or a case study.
93

1	# Copy Templates
2	
3	Use this file for homepage copy direction. Templates are not fixed copy; they are shape, purpose, and guardrails.
4	
5	## 01. Intro
6	
7	| Item | Direction |
8	|---|---|
9	| Section job | Invite the user into the journey |
10	| Reader state | First visual contact |
11	| Message to land | This is a digital launch point |
12	| Shape | short English headline + 2 Korean lines |
13	| Avoid | abstract space fantasy |
14	
15	Example:
16	
17	```text
18	WE DESIGN YOUR JOURNEY
19	브랜드가 처음 세상과 만나는 순간,
20	웹은 가장 선명한 출발점이 됩니다.
21	```
22	
23	## 02. introAction
24	
25	| Item | Direction |
26	|---|---|
27	| Section job | Align with the client and move toward launch |
28	| Reader state | Accepted the start |
29	| Message to land | We start beside you and turn direction into structure |
30	| Shape | two short beats |
31	| Avoid | overusing mission/signal language |
32	
33	## 03. Hero
34	
35	| Item | Direction |
36	|---|---|
37	| Section job | Land the slogan |
38	| Reader state | Direction has become motion |
39	| Message to land | The journey starts on the web |
40	| Shape | `JOIN THE JOURNEY` + short Korean clarification |
41	| Avoid | remixing the slogan |
42	
43	## 04. Story
44	
45	| Item | Direction |
46	|---|---|
47	| Section job | Reveal belief and rejected convention |
48	| Reader state | The journey has started |
49	| Message to land | A new brand cannot rely on default answers |
50	| Shape | belief headline + concrete Korean proof |
51	| Avoid | process lists, service lists, tech lists |
52	
53	## 05. Who
54	
55	| Item | Direction |
56	|---|---|
57	| Section job | Clarify client role and NINEONELABS role |
58	| Reader state | Understands the philosophy |
59	| Message to land | The client leads; NINEONELABS builds the route and structure |
60	| Shape | partnership headline + role-defining Korean body |
61	| Avoid | making NINEONELABS the hero / stripping journey language for transactional phrases |
62	
63	English headline direction: combine client-centric language with journey vocabulary.
64	`YOUR BRAND LEADS. WE BUILD THE ROUTE.` — `LEADS` = client is the main character, `ROUTE` = journey language + NINEONELABS role.
65	
66	Example:
67	
68	```text
69	YOUR BRAND LEADS. WE BUILD THE ROUTE.
70	브랜드의 방향은 클라이언트가 정합니다.
71	우리는 그 방향을 실제 웹 구조와 화면으로 구현합니다.
72	같은 여정 안에서, 함께 움직입니다.
73	```
74	
75	## 06. Why / Skills
76	
77	| Item | Direction |
78	|---|---|
79	| Section job | Earn trust through capability and proof |
80	| Reader state | Knows our role |
81	| Message to land | We have the tools and systems to build the journey |
82	| Shape | compact skill labels + short proof descriptors |
83	| Avoid | service explanations, generic persuasion |
84	
85	Example:
86	
87	```text
88	THREE.JS / INTERACTIVE WEB
89	GSAP / MOTION & ANIMATION
90	CMS SYSTEM / CONTENT CONTROL
91	```
92	
93	## 07. Services
94	
95	| Item | Direction |
96	|---|---|
97	| Section job | Name what we actually ship |
98	| Reader state | Trust is established |
99	| Message to land | NINEONELABS builds web, app, brand, UI/UX, and maintenance systems |
100	| Shape | service category + concise outcome copy |
101	| Avoid | raw technology list, brand philosophy |
102	
103	## 08. Portfolio Intro
104	
105	| Item | Direction |
106	|---|---|
107	| Section job | Prepare evidence |
108	| Reader state | Understands deliverables |
109	| Message to land | The work became real |
110	| Shape | short proof-oriented transition |
111	| Avoid | vague gallery language |
112	
113	## 09. Portfolio Detail
114	
115	| Item | Direction |
116	|---|---|
117	| Section job | Show selected work |
118	| Reader state | Ready for evidence |
119	| Message to land | This is how the system behaves in real work |
120	| Shape | project title + problem/result angle |
121	| Avoid | screenshots with no reason |
122	
123	Example:
124	
125	```text
126	FROM PLAN TO SCREEN
127	WORK BECOMES REAL
128	설계하던 구조와 경험이 이제 실제 화면과 사용 흐름으로 공개됩니다.
129	```
130	
131	## 10. Portfolio Gallery
132	
133	| Item | Direction |
134	|---|---|
135	| Section job | Let evidence accumulate |
136	| Reader state | Has seen one proof point |
137	| Message to land | This is a repeatable standard |
138	| Shape | visual proof with minimal text |
139	| Avoid | over-explaining every item |
140	
141	## 11. Clients / Partners
142	
143	| Item | Direction |
144	|---|---|
145	| Section job | Build trust |
146	| Reader state | Work is proven |
147	| Message to land | Other brands have joined the journey |
148	| Shape | direct title (`PARTNERS` or `CLIENTS`) + trust line + brand list |
149	| Avoid | inflated partnership claims, metaphor-heavy titles for simple logo lists |
150	
151	## 12. Contact
152	
153	| Item | Direction |
154	|---|---|
155	| Section job | Convert interest into a signal |
156	| Reader state | Ready to act |
157	| Message to land | The next journey can begin now |
158	| Temperature | Poetic — maintain the brand voice fully |
159	| Shape | Journey-persona Korean body + direct CTA button labels |
160	| Avoid | Stripping journey language for transactional phrases like "지금 연락하세요" |
161	| CTA rule | CTA button labels are direct (`Contact`, `Works`). Body copy stays in journey voice. |
162	
163	The body copy must be journey-persona but include one concrete digital action or outcome.
164	Wrong: `새로운 여정을 위한 길은 열려 있습니다.` — passive, no action
165	Wrong: `새 프로젝트가 있다면, 지금 연락하세요.` — transactional, no persona
166	Right: Journey language + specific digital word + active verb
167	
168	Example:
169	
170	```text
171	YOUR JOURNEY STARTS HERE.
172	브랜드의 다음 여정이 시작될 때,
173	우리는 그 첫 번째 화면을 함께 설계합니다.
174	```
175

1	# Identity
2	
3	## Brand Identity
4	
5	NINEONELABS is a digital web agency in Korea. We build websites, apps, brand systems, UI/UX, and maintenance systems from first brief to long after launch.
6	
7	The space metaphor is the creative layer. It communicates scale, ambition, and unknown territory. The service, always and without exception, is digital web work.
8	
9	When someone reads NINEONELABS copy, they should understand:
10	
11	1. This team builds digital products.
12	2. They build them through experiment, challenge, and proof.
13	3. The client's brand is the main character.
14	
15	| Item | Rule |
16	|---|---|
17	| Name (EN display) | `NINEONELABS` |
18	| Name (technical lowercase) | `nineonelabs` |
19	| Name (KR) | `나인원랩스` |
20	| Type | Digital Web Agency |
21	| Location | Korea |
22	
23	## Core Values
24	
25	| Value | Korean | In Practice |
26	|---|---|---|
27	| Experiment | 실험 | We prototype interaction systems before production code. |
28	| Challenge | 도전 | We take undefined briefs and turn them into defined outcomes. |
29	| Proof | 증명 | Claims must be demonstrated through shipped work, measurable results, or concrete systems. |
30	
31	## Slogan
32	
33	```text
34	JOIN THE JOURNEY
35	```
36	
37	Usage:
38	
39	| Context | Form |
40	|---|---|
41	| Hero headline / primary CTA | `JOIN THE JOURNEY` |
42	| Section anchors / subheadlines | `Join The Journey` only when title case is visually required |
43	| Korean formal | `함께 여정을 씁니다` |
44	| Korean CTA | `지금, 여정을 시작하세요` |
45	| Korean partnership | `같은 여정을 함께 걷습니다` |
46	
47	Never abbreviate, paraphrase, or remix the slogan in display contexts.
48	
49	## Narrative
50	
51	The brand metaphor is a voyage from where a brand is today to where it has never been before. That destination is **Planet NX-2**, a metaphor for unrealized brand potential.
52	
53	NINEONELABS is not the captain. We are the 조력자: companion, crew, facilitator, and engineering team. The client leads the brand story; we design and build the vessel that carries it.
54	
55	Use the three-stage process:
56	
57	| Stage | Meaning |
58	|---|---|
59	| Discover | Map the brand's current coordinates: strategy, research, brief clarity |
60	| Build | Design and engineer the digital experience: web, app, brand system |
61	| Orbit | Continue after launch: maintenance, iteration, performance, growth |
62	
63	## Services
64	
65	Detailed service manifests live in `services.md`. Keep this section as the quick map only.
66	
67	| Label | Deliverables | Korean Direction |
68	|---|---|---|
69	| WEB | Immersive marketing sites, campaign pages, Three.js interactive experiences, landing pages | 브랜드만의 인터랙션으로 오래 기억되는 웹을 설계합니다. |
70	| APP | React / Flutter apps, PWA, dashboards, hybrid apps | 손 안에서도 이어지는 브랜드 흐름을 만듭니다. |
71	| BRANDING | Logo systems, guidelines, visual language, naming, tone | 브랜드를 한 문장으로 설명할 수 있는 정체성을 만듭니다. |
72	| UI/UX | Wireframes, prototypes, design systems, user research, flows | 사용자가 자연스럽게 다음 행동으로 이동하게 설계합니다. |
73	| MAINTENANCE | Performance audits, CMS, bug fixes, stability SLA, iteration | 출시 이후에도 안정적으로 움직이는 시스템을 운영합니다. |
74	
75	## Technology Strengths
76	
77	Detailed proof structure lives in `proof-system.md`. Use this section as the quick capability map only.
78	
79	Use technology as proof, not decoration.
80	
81	| Technology | Why It Matters |
82	|---|---|
83	| Three.js | Immersive 3D lives inside the production site. |
84	| GSAP | Motion serves story, clarity, and conversion. |
85	| Webflow / CMS | Clients can manage structured content. |
86	| UI/UX Design | Every screen has a job. |
87	| Branding System | Identity works across web, print, motion, and app. |
88	| TypeScript | Fewer bugs at launch, faster iteration after. |
89	| PHP Custom MVC | Backend ownership without unnecessary platform dependency. |
90	
91	## What We Are Not
92	
93	| Avoid | Instead |
94	|---|---|
95	| Aerospace company | Digital web agency with space-as-metaphor |
96	| Abstract art studio | Immersive web studio with defined deliverables |
97	| Generic creative agency | Results-driven team with Experiment · Challenge · Proof |
98	| Space-themed portfolio only | Web agency using space as storytelling language |
99

1	# Positioning
2	
3	Use this file when writing why NINEONELABS should be chosen over another option.
4	
5	## Core Position
6	
7	NINEONELABS is for brands that need a digital experience built around identity, interaction, and proof. We are not the cheapest production option and not a slow corporate agency. We are the crew that walks the brand's journey beside the client and turns undefined brand ambition into a working web/app/brand system.
8	
9	## Versus Cheaper Freelancer
10	
11	### What They Offer
12	
13	- lower cost
14	- fast production
15	- narrower execution
16	
17	### Where They Fail
18	
19	- strategy, brand, UI/UX, and engineering often split apart
20	- long-term operation may be unsupported
21	- identity can become template-like
22	
23	### NINEONELABS Position
24	
25	We connect brand direction, screen structure, motion, implementation, and post-launch operation in one journey.
26	
27	### Copy Angle
28	
29	Choose NINEONELABS when the site must explain the brand, not just exist online.
30	
31	### What Not To Say
32	
33	- freelancers are cheap and bad
34	- we are premium because we cost more
35	
36	## Versus Larger Agency
37	
38	### What They Offer
39	
40	- scale
41	- process
42	- broad teams
43	
44	### Where They Fail
45	
46	- slow decisions
47	- layers between strategy and execution
48	- interaction details can become handoff artifacts
49	
50	### NINEONELABS Position
51	
52	We keep strategy, design, interaction, and build close enough for the work to stay sharp.
53	
54	### Copy Angle
55	
56	The people who define the journey also shape the screen.
57	
58	### What Not To Say
59	
60	- large agencies are careless
61	- we do everything faster
62	
63	## Versus Template / Webflow-Only Build
64	
65	### What They Offer
66	
67	- speed
68	- low friction
69	- manageable content
70	
71	### Where They Fail
72	
73	- brand distinction is limited
74	- interaction is often generic
75	- structure follows the template, not the brand
76	
77	### NINEONELABS Position
78	
79	We use tools when they serve the brand, but the brand never bends to the template. The route belongs to the brand; the tools follow.
80	
81	### Copy Angle
82	
83	Default is safe. Uncharted is where brands begin. 템플릿이 아닌, 브랜드의 여정을 함께 그립니다.
84	
85	### What Not To Say
86	
87	- templates are useless
88	- no-code is not real work
89	
90	## Versus Generic Design Studio
91	
92	### What They Offer
93	
94	- visuals
95	- identity exploration
96	- presentation polish
97	
98	### Where They Fail
99	
100	- digital behavior may be underdefined
101	- web performance and implementation can be secondary
102	- design may not survive production
103	
104	### NINEONELABS Position
105	
106	We design identity as a working digital system: screens, interaction, content, and operation. After launch, we stay in orbit — keeping the system stable through ongoing maintenance.
107	
108	### Copy Angle
109	
110	Not decoration. A brand system that works on the web. 디자인을 넘기고 끝나지 않고, 운영 궤도까지 함께 갑니다.
111	
112	### What Not To Say
113	
114	- design studios only decorate
115	- engineering matters more than design
116	
117	## Positioning Rules
118	
119	- Do not insult competitors.
120	- Compare through client risk, not ego.
121	- Always return to the concrete digital outcome.
122	- If the comparison does not help the client decide, remove it.
123

1	# Homepage Flow
2	
3	The homepage must read as one designed sequence. Each section needs a job, a previous beat, and a next beat.
4	
5	## Narrative Order
6	
7	1. Intro
8	2. introAction
9	3. Hero
10	4. Story
11	5. Who
12	6. Why / Skills
13	7. Services
14	8. Portfolio
15	9. Partners
16	10. Contact
17	
18	## Arc Grouping
19	
20	- `기`: `intro`, `introAction`
21	- `승`: `hero`, `story`, `who`
22	- `전`: `why`, `services`
23	- `결`: `portfolio`, `partners`, `contact`
24	
25	## Scene Context Map
26	
27	| # | Section Class | Scene | Arc Role | Previous Beat | Current Job | Next Beat |
28	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
29	| 01 | `no-main-intro` | `intro` | 기 | First visual contact | Invite the user into the brand journey | The launch sequence begins |
30	| 02 | `no-main-intro-action` | `introAction` | 기 -> 승 | The user has accepted the start | Begin beside the client and turn direction into structure | The slogan lands as shared commitment |
31	| 03 | `no-main-hero` | `hero` | 승 | Direction has become motion | Land `JOIN THE JOURNEY` and clarify that the journey happens through web experience | Explain the philosophy |
32	| 04 | `no-main-story` | `story` | 승 -> 전 | The journey starts on the web | Express company belief, values, or rejected convention | Reframe client as main character |
33	| 05 | `no-main-who` | `who` | 승 -> 전 | The philosophy is established | Clarify the client role and NINEONELABS role | Prove capability through skills |
34	| 06 | `no-main-why` | `whyus` | 전 | Our role is clear | Show proof through technology and capability | Move from capability to deliverables |
35	| 07 | `no-main-services` | `services` | 전 -> 결 | Proof is established | Name what we actually ship | Show real work |
36	| 08 | `no-main-portfolio-intro` | `works` | 결 | Services are concrete | Prepare evidence | Enter portfolio detail |
37	| 09 | `no-main-portfolio` | `worksDetail` | 결 | Evidence begins | Show selected work | Expand proof |
38	| 10 | `no-main-portfolio-gallery` | `worksFinal` | 결 | Work has been shown | Let evidence accumulate | Move to trust signals |
39	| 11 | `no-main-clients` | `client` | 결 | Work is proven | Show who trusted the journey | Open contact |
40	| 12 | `no-main-contact` | `contact` | 결 -> new 기 | Trust is established | Convert interest into a signal or brief | A new journey begins |
41	
42	## Section Definitions
43	
44	For section copy shape and examples, use `copy-templates.md`. For section judgment, use `review-algorithm.md`.
45	
46	| Section | Must Contain | Must Not Become |
47	|---|---|---|
48	| `story` | company belief, values, convention rejected | process list, tech proof, service list |
49	| `who` | client's role and NINEONELABS role | tech proof list |
50	| `why` | capability and proof | deliverable catalog |
51	| `services` | concrete deliverables | brand philosophy |
52	| `portfolio` | evidence | abstract inspiration |
53	| `contact` | clear next action | poetic closure without action |
54	
55	## Implementation Comment Rule
56	
57	- The detailed HTML comment directly above each homepage `section` in `views/pages/index.php` is the implementation-level version of this document's Scene Context Map.
58	- Each comment should include `SCENE`, `ARC`, `PREVIOUS BEAT`, `CURRENT JOB`, `VISUAL CONTEXT`, `COPY RULE`, and `NEXT BEAT`.
59	- When updating homepage copy, align the code comment with this file first or in the same change.
60	- If a section has no comment yet, derive it from this document's arc and section job before writing or revising copy.
61	
62	## Visual Context Notes
63	
64	| Section | Visual Context | Copy Direction |
65	|---|---|---|
66	| `no-main-who` | The origin is visible after launch | Do not name the visual literally unless needed. Use the scene to imply moving beyond the starting point together. Clarify that the client leads the journey and NINEONELABS builds the next web structure. |
67	| `no-main-portfolio` | Looking through a spacecraft window | Use the window as proof framing: the work is now outside the plan, visible, launched, and real. Avoid space description for its own sake. |
68	
69	## Why And Services Boundary
70	
71	For detailed service content, use `services.md`. For proof language, use `proof-system.md`.
72	
73	| Section | Role | Good Content | Avoid |
74	|---|---|---|---|
75	| `no-main-why` | reason to choose NINEONELABS | skills, technology strengths, proof signals, capability labels | long service explanations, generic persuasion, poetic mission copy |
76	| `no-main-services` | what NINEONELABS actually ships | concrete deliverables, service categories, short outcome descriptions | raw technology list, vague capability claims, brand philosophy |
77	
78	`why` earns trust. `services` names the work. Keep these two jobs separate.
79	
80	## Story Arc Rules
81	
82	- Every section must answer what changed since the previous section.
83	- Every section must create anticipation for the next section.
84	- Do not repeat the same emotional beat twice in a row.
85	- A headline may be poetic, but body copy must make practical meaning clear.
86	- If a section uses metaphor, the next sentence must ground it in web, app, branding, UI/UX, maintenance, process, or proof.
87	
88	## Example: `no-main-story`
89	
90	- Position: section 04.
91	- Scene: `story`.
92	- Previous: `hero` says the journey starts on the web.
